name: Shamma
overview: Shamma was a male member of the tribe of Asher, identified in Scripture as the son of Zophah. His mention is brief and specific, highlighting his lineage within the tribe. There are no additional notes or details about his life or role beyond this genealogical reference.
namesAndTitles: The name Shamma means "astonishment" in Hebrew. This proper name is recorded without indication that it was given by God, simply serving as his personal identifier in Scripture.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Shamma as the son of Zophah. Beyond this paternal relationship, no further family connections are documented in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Shamma's significance lies primarily in his place within the genealogical records of the tribe of Asher, as noted in 1 Chronicles 7:37. These genealogies serve to preserve the heritage and identity of God's people, linking individuals to their tribal origins. While Shamma himself is not described as playing a direct role in Israel's narrative, his inclusion underscores the faithfulness of God in maintaining the lineage of His chosen tribes.
